title: Comparing the dataset with SAG
text: summary stock dataset calculated FLStock object. spawning stock biomass, mean fishing mortality recruitment come model estimates. catches SAG usually observed catches, catches come observed data dataset , estimates otherwise.
code: # The summary of a stock assessment in the dataset. # # Returns a data frame with one row per quantity and year.  dataset_summary <- function(stock_code, assessment_year) {   estimated <- stockpile_flstock(stock_code, assessment_year, type = "estimated")   version <- stockpile_stocks(stock_code, assessment_year)   catches <- if (version$observed) {     catch(stockpile_flstock(stock_code, assessment_year, type = "observed"))   } else {     catch(estimated)   }    quantities <- list(SSB = ssb(estimated), F = fbar(estimated), recruitment = rec(estimated), catches = catches)   rows <- lapply(names(quantities), function(quantity) {     values <- as.data.frame(quantities[[quantity]])     data.frame(quantity = quantity, year = values$year, dataset = values$data)   })   do.call(rbind, rows) }  # The summary of a stock assessment in SAG, in the same layout.  sag_summary <- function(stock_code, assessment_year) {   sag <- getSAG(stock_code, assessment_year)   rows <- lapply(c("SSB", "F", "recruitment", "catches"), function(quantity) {     data.frame(quantity = quantity, year = sag$Year, sag = sag[[quantity]])   })   do.call(rbind, rows) }  # The two summaries side by side, for the years and quantities in both.  compare_summaries <- function(stock_code, assessment_year) {   both <- merge(dataset_summary(stock_code, assessment_year), sag_summary(stock_code, assessment_year))   both <- both[!is.na(both$dataset) & !is.na(both$sag) & both$sag != 0, ]   both$ratio <- both$dataset / both$sag   both[order(both$quantity, both$year), ] }

code: stocks <- stockpile_stocks() stocks <- stocks[stocks$estimated, ] stocks$simple <- stocks$n_seasons == 1 & stocks$n_units == 1 & stocks$n_areas == 1  comparisons <- lapply(which(stocks$simple), function(i) {   compared <- try(compare_summaries(stocks$stock_code[i], stocks$assessment_year[i]), silent = TRUE)   if (inherits(compared, "try-error") || nrow(compared) == 0) {     return(NULL)   }   cbind(stock_code = stocks$stock_code[i], assessment_year = stocks$assessment_year[i], compared) }) comparisons <- do.call(rbind, comparisons)  stocks$compared <- paste(stocks$stock_code, stocks$assessment_year) %in%   paste(comparisons$stock_code, comparisons$assessment_year) agreement <- aggregate(   ratio ~ stock_code + assessment_year + quantity, comparisons,   function(ratio) max(abs(ratio - 1)) < 0.025 ) names(agreement)[4] <- "same"  table(agreement$quantity, ifelse(agreement$same, "same", "different")) #>               #>               different same #>   catches            14   12 #>   F                   7   29 #>   recruitment         7   27 #>   SSB                 5   31 all_same <- aggregate(same ~ stock_code + assessment_year, agreement, all)

code: stocks <- stockpile_stocks()  stock_database <- lapply(unique(stocks$assessment_year), function(year) {   sd <- getSD(year = year)   data.frame(     stock_code = sd$StockKeyLabel,     assessment_year = year,     expert_group = sd$ExpertGroup,     data_category = sd$DataCategory,     species = sd$SpeciesCommonName   ) }) stock_database <- do.call(rbind, stock_database)  stocks <- merge(stocks, stock_database, all.x = TRUE) stocks$expert_group[is.na(stocks$expert_group)] <- "not in the stock database"  # what the dataset has for each stock assessment stocks$contents <- ifelse(   stocks$observed & stocks$estimated, "observed and estimated",   ifelse(stocks$estimated, "estimated only", "observed only") ) stocks$contents <- factor(stocks$contents, c("observed and estimated", "estimated only", "observed only"))  # a label for each stock assessment stocks$assessment <- paste0(stocks$stock_code, " (", stocks$assessment_year, ")")  contents_colours <- c("observed and estimated" = "#1b9e77", "estimated only" = "#7570b3", "observed only" = "#d95f02") ggplot(stocks, aes(y = reorder(expert_group, expert_group, length), fill = contents)) +   geom_bar() +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = function(limits) seq(0, limits[2], by = 2)) +   scale_fill_manual(values = contents_colours) +   labs(x = "stock assessments in the dataset", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")
